description:
Pre-existing; uncovered by fz-5xp.57, which is what first let a binary over
64 bytes match a pattern at all on the native doors.

MINIMAL REPRODUCER -- `run` only, interp is clean:

    fn main() do
      dbg(walk(<65 'a's>, 0))
      dbg(walk(<70 'b's>, 0))
    end
    fnp walk(<<_c, rest :: binary>>, n), do: walk(rest, n + 1)
    fnp walk(_b, n), do: n

    stdout: 65, 70    -- correct
    exit:   138       -- SIGBUS, silently, after main finishes

THE TRIGGER IS EXACT:

    two big literals, never matched  ->  exit 0
    one big literal, walked          ->  exit 0
    one big + one small, walked      ->  exit 0
    TWO big literals, both walked    ->  exit 138

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG. At shutdown, mso_drop_all_deferred walks the MSO chain
and releases each ProcBin's SharedBin. One surviving stub's shared_ptr is not a
SharedBin at all -- it is the ADDRESS OF `shared_bin_destructor_noop`:

    P TEARDOWN stub=0x90b4c4020 sb=0x101fe7a00 rc=17942349577604580351
               bit_len=15447069372505408511 bytes_ptr=0xf90007e0d100c3ff
               dtor=0xaa0103e8f90013e8
               noop=0x101fe7a00     <-- sb == the noop destructor's address

Reading 'fields' off a function pointer gives machine code, and the release then
does a refcount fetch_sub into read-only executable memory:

    stop reason = EXC_BAD_ACCESS (code=2, address=0x101283650)
    frame #0: core::sync::atomic::atomic_sub::<usize, usize>

code=2 is a protection failure -- a WRITE to memory that is not writable.

The stub is not corrupted later: its word0 is the same value at mso_sweep time
and at teardown. It was already wrong when it was made.

WHERE TO LOOK. Only compiler-baked static SharedBins are involved
(src/ir_codegen/aot_main.rs define_static_sharedbin, called from
native_codegen/prim.rs ConstBitstring). The struct's destructor field at +32 is
a function-address relocation to shared_bin_destructor_noop, and the value that
ends up in the ProcBin is exactly that relocation's target -- so the suspicion is
that the second `.fz_bs_sb_N` data symbol's address, or the relocation applied
to it, resolves to +32 of a neighbouring object. The two statics are emitted
adjacent (observed at 0xc43270000 and 0xc43270028, exactly 40 bytes apart, with
no padding).

NOT VERIFIED, and the next step: dump both static symbols' resolved addresses and
their 40 bytes after finalize_definitions, and compare with the sb_ptr each
fz_alloc_procbin_from_static call receives.

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE: no fixture had a binary literal over 64 bytes that was
matched, because until fz-5xp.57 matching one was impossible. It is also silent
in release -- the process just exits 138 after printing the right answers.
title: Two matched binary literals over 64 bytes corrupt a ProcBin and die at teardown on run
